renderPage/renderTextLayer build the viewport with scale only
the render effect and its rotation prop

scope: One container component, its wiring into DocumentViewer, and the rotation argument in the pdf render helpers. Out of scope: scroll-driven cursors, thumbnails, per-page zoom.

acceptance_criteria.text: Stepping the cursor slides the mounted page window and disables the control at each bound.
Rotate dispatches rotated and the rendered canvas changes shape.
page-controls.test.tsx covers indicator, bounds and rotate; use-page-stage.test.ts covers the rotation argument.
README, the review and the vault cache record it.

open_questions: Whether the page cursor should also follow scrolling (an IntersectionObserver over the mounted pages) is a UX choice, left open; the control is the smallest honest dispatcher today.
risks: A rotation change re-renders the page; the abort signal from 033 already cancels the previous paint, so the two do not collide.
The window is cursor-based, so a 2-page document always mounts both pages and only the indicator moves — expected, and covered by the 4-page fixture.
